title: Asymmetric Light Scattering from an Atomic System with Gain: A Quantum Analysis
abstract: We study the the scattering of light by a binary system of identical atoms in which one of them is incoherently pumped. This system belongs to the kind of non-parity symmetric optical systems in which gains and losses are partially compensated. We carry out a fully quantum analysis of the directionality of the radiation scattered from the atoms when the incident light strikes the system either perpendicular or alongside the interatomic axis. We find that, generally, while the degree of asymmetry depends on the pump rate, the preferred direction for emission depends on the interatomic distance and the detuning of the probe field with respect to the resonant frequency. On physical grounds, for the case of frontal illumination, the asymmetry is the result of the interference of the photons emitted from different atoms. On the contrary, for side lighting, the asymmetry with respect to the side of incidence is caused by both the phase difference between the probe field photons that strike each atom and the interference between the photons emitted from different atoms. Further, for side lighting too, our quantum approach demonstrates that the forward scattered power depends on the side of incidence, which reveals the lack of reciprocity in the quantum optical response of the system. This result conflicts with what is obtained within a classical approach.
summary: The paper provides a rigorous quantum analysis of asymmetric light scattering from two interacting atoms with built-in gain. It demonstrates that the system exhibits non-reciprocal behavior, meaning the scattered power depends on whether the incident light approaches from the 'gain' or 'loss' side. This quantum finding directly contradicts predictions made by classical linear response theories.
main_problem: The study investigates the directionality (asymmetry) of light scattering from a binary atomic system that incorporates gain, comparing quantum predictions against classical linear response theories.
main_result: The fully quantum analysis reveals a lack of reciprocity in the optical response for side lighting, showing an asymmetry dependent on the incidence side and detuning, which contradicts classical expectations.
method: The authors employ a time-dependent perturbation theory within the wavefunction formalism, calculating scattering power using diagrammatic expansions (e.g., Dyson series) to account for quantum interference effects.
model_or_system: The system is a binary dimer of identical atoms, where one atom is incoherently pumped (creating gain/loss mechanisms) and interacts with incident and scattered photons via the dipole coupling Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Differential scattering power ($W_{sc}(	heta)$), forward vs. backward scattered power ratios ($ rac{W_{fw}^G}{W_{fw}^L}$), and angular distribution asymmetry.
important_parameters: Pump rate, detuning of the probe field ($\omega - \omega_0$), interatomic distance ($R$), and the ratio of gain/loss coupling strengths.
main_assumptions: Approximations include assuming the dipole moment lies perpendicular to the interatomic axis, using steady-state limits ($\gamma t \gg 1$), and distinguishing between single-atom and collective (both-atoms) scattering processes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate angular distributions of scattered power for frontal vs. side illumination, showing ratios of forward/backward powers as functions of detuning and pump rate, comparing quantum results to classical predictions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives expressions for differential scattering power ($W$) in different geometries (frontal $\perp$, side $G$, side $L$), contrasting the quantum calculation (using diagrams) with the classical linear response theory prediction at each stage.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it explores non-linear, non-reciprocal light scattering phenomena in open quantum systems driven by gain/loss mechanisms. The conflict between quantum and classical predictions highlights fundamental limitations of semiclassical approximations.

Partially Pumped Collective Emitters.note: The core concept of the new paper—analyzing scattering from a binary system where one atom is incoherently pumped (creating gain/loss)—directly mirrors the physics of partial pumping and local drive asymmetry in collective emitters.
